how: Starting is distributed across a missing-logo question and anonymous placement plans rather than attributable to one confirmed founder.
Placement plans and renewed calls invite members to build and defend the logo.
Members answer the placement proposal with bare commitments to join.
A participant judges available resources insufficient to maintain both the main logo and the rival slogan.
A starter's plan can itself be the call for hands, so a distinct later recruitment step is not established.
A placement plan receives a reply reporting a tile placed for the group, supporting participation beyond verbal assent.
Bare acceptance is observed in replies to a plan, but those replies cannot establish an obligation for every reader or a general preference structure.
Resource shortage must be attached to the particular work because members can prioritize the core logo over an optional slogan without relocating.
A larger replacement is proposed conditionally, while the explicit abandonment report concerns the rival's logo rather than a confirmed relocation of this room.
Members specify the logo's colours and location and propose a black rectangular background.
An edited rebuilding account reports completed letters and remaining work while the logo changes under attack.
Defense calls combine direct canvas coordinates and a blueprint showing the intended logo.
A shared target must be paired with refreshing the canvas before builders can recognize the current damage and correct their placements.
Instruction includes learning the repeat-placement wait and recovering from a misplaced tile.
The room routes defenders to a named Discord channel alongside the blueprint while keeping the call and resources visible in the thread.
Surviving placement directions and later blueprints do not preserve a design argument being settled by posting the template.
Visible instructions do not establish whether formal ordering was decided inside the linked chat, and one room cannot test the cross-room frequency claim.
A member reports signing into all their alts to repair unwanted colours while finding the damage too extensive.
The request to copy a protection script supports proposed automation only, whereas extra-account use is explicitly reported elsewhere.
Learning the ten-minute wait does not instantiate added placements through scripts, bots or spare accounts.
The same report connects overwhelming unwanted colours to using alts for additional repairs.
Members repeatedly call for backup, rebuild the letters and recommit to defending the completed logo.
The edited account explicitly carries letter completion through further attacks to defending the finished logo.
Candidate attribution is locally necessary because participants check placers and distinguish mistaken repairs, uninformed neighbours and alleged rival teams.
Choosing what to repair and whom to blame depends on distinguishing intended fixes and neighbours' plans from hostile pixels, without making every accusation accurate.
Neighbours discuss a one-block adjustment, apologize for crossed borders and report a truce.
A member reports carrying a request to move down one block to the neighbouring subreddit.
A neighbour apologizes for pushing the logo down and the room accepts because sufficient space remains.
Neighbour accommodation includes offering defense, thanking the offer and answering a request for help.
The neighbour's appeal explicitly connects crossing the defended border with seeking an adjustment that lets both logos coexist.
A truce supplies a line to respect only insofar as individual placers learn it, requiring messages and announcements when uninformed fans continue crossing.
A participant reports helping the rival logo while judging both small subs too weak to compete, supporting help amid strain without proving a collective pact.
Accepting an apology over displaced space is answered by a conditional offer of defense and then thanks.
The stated compliance problem is uninformed fans missing a truce, without an observed assertion that its maker cannot bind them.
Border talk leads visibly to communicating the truce, while a subsequent dispute over who may commit the room remains unobserved.
Help offers and neighbour accommodation do not establish coalition membership or an agreement to defend each other.
Defense and a neighbour's help offer are visible, but a resulting coalition is not established.
The request describes adjacent logos coexisting after a one-block move rather than a host governing a guest mark.
Team rivalry supplies the named opponent in contempt for a rival logo and a proposal to destroy it.
Existing fan attachments appear in collective victory language and an attempted birthday tribute replacing the rival slogan.
A team rival is named in the same surviving title that proposes destroying its canvas work.
Naming a rival does not identify every attacker because one admitted saboteur identifies with another team and reports recruitment by a rival fan.
Members interpret a player's worrying post through April Fools and discuss rival subreddit jokes alongside their own unchanged layout.
Tagged resubmissions and removal nodes show posting-rule encounters but do not establish a canvas-specific boundary or a new moderation policy.
Removal beneath a placement call does not establish that calls flooded the subreddit or caused its posting rules.
Members announce that they did it and congratulate the builders.
Members preserve a perfect-form image before an expected ending and later recount survival with a blemish.
The completed-work announcement receives congratulations from a builder-facing reply.
Recording a perfect version before an expected ending can precede resumed upkeep rather than a completed transition away from defense.
When the anticipated shutdown fails to arrive, the author explicitly returns from preserving the perfect logo to requesting more defense.
Accounts of a blemished finish and an interrupted live redesign do not establish a dispute over cleaning a retained historical canvas.
The visible closing thanks record survival but do not establish a proposal to carry the effort into a lasting venue or emblem.
A closing record is present but no evidenced continuation decision permits testing whether recording generated one.
The record contains a direct call to destroy the rival's work and a participant's report of trying to overtake a restored design.
An admitted saboteur receives a fan's victory claim and replies with an account of rival recruitment.
A later attack proposal does not show that an earlier building call brought its author to the canvas or redirected the room's hands.
The attack title has no retained member refusal, and an earlier separate objection to covering the rival cannot serve as its answer.
The rival attack proposal and a different neighbour's later truce are not connected by a passage answering the proposal.
An admission of all-day sabotage is directly answered by a victory claim, carrying the attack into a spoken contest.
Maintaining the core logo is explicitly prioritized over maintaining a rival slogan when members judge resources inadequate for both.
